detailed_description: Checksum Verifier calculates file hashes in the browser and compares them with an expected value. Pick a file up to 100 MB through the file picker, optionally paste an expected checksum, then click Calculate to compute MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, and SHA-512 in parallel using the Web Crypto API. If an expected value is set, the tool automatically reports which of those four algorithms it matches, or that there is no match. Each calculated hash can be copied to the clipboard, and Clear resets the file and result. It does not provide drag-and-drop upload, algorithm selection, hashing of pasted text, batch files, or HMAC variants.
usage_steps: Click the upload area and select a file up to 100 MB
Optionally paste an expected checksum into the input field
Click Calculate and wait for the browser to finish hashing
Review the MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, and SHA-512 values listed in the results
Check the match banner that names the matched algorithm or reports no match
Copy any individual hash with its Copy button, or click Clear to reset
usage_examples: Verify a downloaded installer against a SHA-256 value published on the vendor's site
Check whether a file was corrupted after a transfer by recomputing its hash locally
Compare two copies of a file by hashing each and comparing the SHA-512 values
Quickly tell which algorithm a published checksum uses by letting the tool match against MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, or SHA-512
